result.title: SGAR: Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction via Sparse Geometry-Guided Attention
result.summary: Feed-forward models have been very successful in 3D reconstruction with ad hoc attention designs that relate all view patches densely. However, the cost of this dense global attention grows quadratically with the number of views, preventing the model from applying to larger-scale reconstruction settings. In this paper, we argue that most dense attention computations are unnecessary from a classical structure-from-motion perspective: 3D structures stem from geometrically matching regions in 2D. We bring this principle to learning-based feed-forward reconstruction with our Sparse Geometric Attention Reconstruction (SGAR) method. In SGAR, each patch token attends to only a small set of patch tokens from other views, chosen by a lightweight learned key selection module trained to predict cross-view 3D proximity of tokens. Thus, dense global attention is replaced by much more efficient geometric-similarity-guided sparse attention. SGAR is a general method that can be applied to different feed-forward models by fine-tuning. In our experiments, we show that SGAR is the fastest among both state-of-the-art dense and sparse methods and the most accurate sparse one. It runs up to 12-times faster than dense attention at 1,000 views with stable pose accuracy where existing sparse methods fail, and shows the best performance in reconstructing more complete geometries on the same time budget.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文针对 feed-forward 三维重建中稠密跨视图注意力的二次复杂度问题，提出 SGAR：用轻量学习的选择模块预测 token 间跨视图三维邻近性，使每个 patch token 只关注少量其他视图 token，从而以稀疏几何引导注意力替代全局稠密注意力。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「学习式稀疏 key 选择」可供核查是否可迁移到 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选与注意力范围控制，即用轻量预测器决定哪些视觉 token 值得进入推理状态；但该工作本身面向三维重建，与多模态推理无直接联系，迁移性属推测。
